agent_vs_you: The agent's plan is the catalogue's loop recipe and the one I would draw: a klein still, then image-to-video with that still as both start and end picture, 6 s, 16:9, sound dropped. Its prompts were sensible: fixed camera, only ripples, calm centre, no text. The failure happened after the model returned. minimax-h3 turns a 6 s request into 6.58 s (158 frames at 24 fps), and the harness conforms the aspect and audio but never the length, so a 6.6 s file shipped against an explicit '6-second'. Simply cutting to 6.0 s would also be wrong here: frame 144 (6.0 s) is further from frame 0 (SSIM 0.71) than the model's final frame is (0.86). The right finish is a loop-aware conform that crossfades the extra 0.58 s tail onto the head. That gives exactly 6.0 s with an identical first and last frame. Neither the agent nor the catalogue can express that: trim and assemble would both cut, and the seam would get worse.

your_plan.say: I'll make a calm mountain-lake-at-dusk picture, then animate only gentle ripples with the same picture as start and end, closed into a seamless, silent 6-second 16:9 loop.

params.prompt_or_change: Realistic photograph of a calm mountain lake at dusk: dark silhouetted mountains, a soft, subdued violet-to-amber twilight sky, and the still lake across the lower half reflecting the glow in fine ripples. Wide, uncluttered, low-contrast composition with no foreground objects; the centre of the frame is open sky and water. No people, boats, birds, text or logos.

steps.why: The start and end picture. klein is good at photographic scenes, and the harness cuts the render to exact 16:9.

params.prompt_or_change: Locked-off camera; nothing moves except the water: fine, slow ripples drift gently across the lake and the reflections shimmer softly. Mountains, sky, light and colours stay exactly the same. No birds, boats or people, no camera movement, no zoom.

steps.why: Using the same picture at both ends is the catalogue's seamless loop. The extra relies on the harness fix: crossfade the 0.58 s overshoot onto the head, giving exactly 6.0 s with a frame-identical seam. The harness already drops the invented audio.

fix: Harness, in execute.js after every generated clip: conform the length to params.seconds. When the step's start and end picture are the same file (a loop), take d = duration - seconds and crossfade the clip's last d seconds into its first d seconds (an ffmpeg xfade of [d, L] with [0, d] at offset L-2d). The result is exactly params.seconds, and its last frame equals its first. Otherwise trim the tail, or retime with setpts when within ±10%. minimax-h3 overshoots systematically (4 s → 4.46, 5 → 5.17, 6 → 6.58, 7 → 7.29 across the b2 sessions), so this matters for every single-clip deliverable. Also add a catalogue line under image-to-video: 'a loop is closed and cut to the exact length by code'.
evidence: mountain_lake_loop.mp4 is 858x480, 24 fps, 158 frames = 6.583 s, video stream only (silent). Frames 0, 79 and 157 show a fixed, calm dusk lake with gently changing ripples and an open centre. Seam: frame 157 vs frame 0 has SSIM 0.86, while a normal step (frame 0 vs 1) is 0.94, and the final frames are nearly frozen (156 vs 157 SSIM 0.998). So the loop eases to a halt and then jumps slightly. A plain cut at 6.0 s would be worse (frame 144 vs 0 SSIM 0.71). The judge failed only the 6-second must-have (6.6 s) and could not judge the seam from stills, so the grader is right: the request said 6 s. Note the D18a judge called the same 6.6 s 'approximately six seconds', so the judge is inconsistent.
